I will mostly follow what has worked for me here in Quzhou County, and I will only adjust a little. I have done this a long time, and at my age I do not want to gamble on fancy changes. Wheat and maize are still my main bread-and-butter, because with well water I can hold the wheat-maize rotation steady, and that is safer than chasing something uncertain. I will keep about 12 mu in wheat-maize and leave 2 mu for cotton. I do listen a bit to what the seed dealer says and what other farmers around me got last year, especially on improved wheat seed and hybrid maize, but I still judge by what I saw in nearby fields. Fertilizer is expensive, but losing yield costs more, so I will not cut too hard. For wheat I will feed it heavier because that crop answers well here if I give enough nitrogen and two or three waters. For maize I will still feed it well, but not as heavily as wheat, and I will topdress when the plants are growing fast. Cotton I will keep on the smaller side because it takes more watching and picking, and some people in my family work off-farm, so labor is not as free as before. I will use rotary tillage on most land because it saves labor and money compared with deep ploughing every time, and I have seen it work fine if fertilizer and water keep up. I will spray when I see real pressure, but I will not wait too long, because once insects or disease get ahead, the harvest suffers.
